defects.summary: A DM can be permanently broken. chat.leave is exposed as "Leave conversation" in DM settings, and chat.removeMember has no group check, so the DM creator (stored as admin) can remove the peer. Either way the pair can never talk again: createDm returns the existing dmPairs channel, where the removed/left user gets NOT_MEMBER, and addMember refuses DMs (GROUP_REQUIRED). The remaining party keeps sending into a channel nobody receives. The removal also revokes the peer's server access to shared DM history.
defects.evidence: trace.md#a8 (grading/evidence/dm-membership.json); snapback/chat.q removeMember/leave/createDm; ui ChatSettingsForm renders "Leave conversation" for non-groups

defects.summary: Link taps call an unbound Linking.openURL (onPressLink={Linking.openURL} in src/posts.tsx, src/profile.tsx, src/chat.tsx). On web every tap throws an uncaught TypeError ("reading '_dispatchEvent'"), and the link opens only because window.open runs first. defects.evidence: trace.md#d-09 — evidence/scale-receipt.json verifications[].timings; grading/logs/probe-o5.json

defects.summary: evidence/scale-receipt.json records `start` and `end` in epoch seconds while every neighbouring timestamp field in the lane’s evidence is epoch milliseconds, so a naive reader renders the replay window as 1970-01-21. The real replay window is ~520 s.
defects.evidence: trace.md#d-10 — evidence/scale-receipt.json start/end

defects.summary: A group message's aggregate receipt advances to 'read by all' when an unread member merely leaves the group, instead of staying pinned to the recipient set as of send time. schema.q's receipt() takes the minimum over rows currently in `members`, so deleting an unread member's membership removes them from the requirement rather than holding the aggregate back.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-01 — three-member group, Bob acknowledges state 2, Carol never reads: aggregate correctly stays 0; Carol then leaves (removeMember on her own membership) and the aggregate jumps to 2 ('read by all') with no one having read her copy. Source: snapback/schema.q:223-229 (fn receipt) with the members delete rule at schema.q:172.

defects.summary: POST /m/acknowledge returns state:"sent" for a caller who is not a member of the message's chat, while performing no change. The only delivery-acknowledgement operation API.md documents therefore reports success for a call it silently ignored, so a custom client cannot tell 'acknowledged' from 'discarded'.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-02 — a freshly registered non-member POSTed /m/acknowledge {ids:["sm0001"],state:2} and received state:"sent"; the message's receipt and all target state were unchanged. Every other non-member write in the same probe was refused terminally (NOT_MEMBER / NOT_ADMIN / MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND / E_RULE). Source: snapback/schema.q:289-302.

defects.summary: The logged notification-provider seam writes to a path it does not create: snapback/worker.mts appends each payload to CLIQUE_PUSH_LOG (default evidence/push.jsonl) without ensuring the directory exists, so on an instance whose log directory is absent every push and digest payload is lost with no visible error while the effect is still acknowledged to the backend.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-03 — observed on a grader-created isolated instance whose working directory had no evidence/ folder: the schedule fired and the digest job ran, but no payload was ever recorded. Creating the directory made the same seam record payloads normally. Does not affect the lane's own evidence, where evidence/ exists. Source: snapback/worker.mts (appendFile on `path` with no mkdir).

defects.summary: The documented acceptance entrypoint is not self-contained for M8: `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m8` fails unless scripts/start-proof.mjs and scripts/trending-proof.mjs have already been run, because the tests mapped to m8-a05/a06/a07 read evidence/m8-trending-clock.json and query the separate clock-offset backend on port 49363. defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#defect-d-04 — I had to start the proof instance and run trending-proof.mjs before the m8 suite would pass on my fresh store; the other six milestones needed nothing beyond backend, seeds and web server. defects.summary: At the scale envelope the trending query answers complete:false with cut:null, and the Trending screen never surfaces it: src/Social.tsx:321-335 branches only on r.data.length, rendering rows as exhaustive or the <TrendingEmpty/> 'no results' state, while the lane's paged surfaces do render 'Results may be incomplete' (src/Social.tsx:40-42). The ranking itself is correct - the grader matched the API's top-5 against read-only SQL ground truth over 48270 in-window top-level posts, exactly and in order - so this is a correctness-honesty and empty-state defect, not wrong data.

defects.summary: An expired disappearing message can still be rendered at the instant a relaunched client opens the conversation, intermittently under load. The grader's first independent run of the frozen M5 choreography segment failed disappearing-message-expiry-and-purge with 'expired message remained visible after both clients relaunched' after the harness's 300 s wait against a 180 s TTL; the second run of the same segment passed, and a faithful instrumented reproduction passed at every step (control applied, server TTL exactly 180000 ms, server point query null, 0 matching bubbles on both clients at +4 s and +20 s). Tally: 1 failure in 3 grader-driven harness attempts, the failing one while 1-minute load climbed past 37. Not a configuration or server fault and not deterministic - most consistent with a race between the relaunched client's local-replica read and its reconciliation of the expiry, which the harness catches because it checks with no tolerance window. It matters because the lane's own green bar (ENVIRONMENT.md) requires the choreography segment to pass for EVERY check, so on that attempt M5 would not have been green; it is minor rather than major because the brief's m5-a02 allows a tolerance for connected clients, no data is wrong, and the server correctly refuses the expired message throughout.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md §4.9 and §6 d-05: grading/work/choreo-grader-m5.jsonl (STRUCTURED CHOREOGRAPHY MISS, attempt 303940.8 ms) versus grading/work/choreo-grader-m5b.jsonl (passed, 304365 ms); grading/work/g-disappear-repro.mjs step log; instrument/choreography/choreography.mjs:2290-2333 with the default adapter's optionValue 24h / waitMs 300000 at lines 65-67.

defects.summary: API.md never names the field carrying a failed mutation's refusal reason. It documents `denied` for queries and says 'A failed receipt or denied must be surfaced', but a failed mutation's reason lives in `why` ({code, family, message, rule, site}), which the document never mentions. A third-party client written from API.md alone can detect the failure but cannot surface its reason - which is what the same paragraph asks it to do. The diagnostics themselves are good; this is purely the documentation gap. The grader hit it directly: a first probe looked for a `failure` field and found null.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md §6 d-04: grading/work/g-refusal.mjs output with four refusal envelopes (NOT_AUTHOR, NOT_MEMBER, E_INPUT, MIXED_MEDIA) all carrying `why`; API.md section 'Request and response envelopes'.

defects.summary: A consumed view-once photo reverts to "unopened" on the recipient’s client after any page reload, and stays that way indefinitely, so the client misreports which view-once photos have already been burned.

defects.summary: At the frozen scale envelope the chat-list (inbox) query was refused server-side: the unread count was an unbounded scan inside the returned shape, and at 100,015 messages the 100% checkpoint failed with E_SHAPE_EXCEEDS_METER. The lane diagnosed it, replaced the raw scan with a row-keyed maintained count, and re-verified - but only after the replay, so the final source generation differs from the one the 10% and 50% checkpoints were measured on, and the three-point growth curve is not a single-generation curve.
defects.evidence: evidence/scale-result-before-unread-fix.json (pass:false, E_SHAPE_EXCEEDS_METER at programs.inbox.2); evidence/scale-source-before-unread-fix.json vs evidence/scale-source-final.json (scale-instance/snapback/schema.q f40a9e9... -> d1bdf39...); evidence/scale-result.json correction field; grading/trace.md#o5

defects.summary: The documented acceptance entrypoint "npm run acceptance -- --milestone m8" fails from a clean start unless a second backend (trend-instance on port 49365, with --replay) has been started by hand first. The entrypoint neither starts nor checks for it, and the failure surfaces as a bare assert(r.ok) AssertionError from trending-proof.mjs with no diagnostic naming the missing instance. The requirement is documented in README.md, so it is recoverable, but every other milestone runs from the entrypoint alone.
defects.evidence: grading/trace.md#phase1 (first m8 acceptance run, AssertionError at scripts/trending-proof.mjs:2); README.md paragraph 3; scripts/trending-proof.mjs hard-codes http://127.0.0.1:49365

defects.summary: Cross-client live updates intermittently exceeded the frozen harness 10 s observation ceiling under shared-machine load. Across the grader runs, 4 of roughly 45 two-client live-update attempts missed: reaction-chip clearing (all 3 attempts in two isolated-segment runs), delete-for-everyone tombstone (1 attempt), video-element readiness (1 attempt). Targeted grader best-of-3 measurement of the same observables did not reproduce it (reaction chip set 798 ms, replace 797 ms, remove 1346 ms; API-driven 1335-3484 ms), and the harness passed the same assertions in the builder receipt and in the grader continuous run, so this is a load-sensitive liveness margin rather than a functional break.
defects.evidence: grading/out/grader-choreo.jsonl; grading/out/grader-choreo-m4-rerun.jsonl; grading/out/grader-choreo-m4-run3.jsonl; grading/out/reaction-ui.json; grading/out/reaction-live.json; uptime load averages 20-27 recorded in grading/trace.md#load

defects.summary: A newly signed-up account can never open the profile editor or the Profile tab, so a new user can never set a display name, handle, bio or avatar. src/ProfileScreen.tsx runs `const targetHandle = handle ?? mine?.handle; if (!targetHandle) return <Text>Loading profile…</Text>;` BEFORE the `if (mode === "edit")` branch, and a fresh account has no profiles row, so both /profile/edit and the Profile tab render 'Loading profile…' forever.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-01 — src/ProfileScreen.tsx:15-21; grading/evidence/shots/dbg-new-account-profile-blocked.png; /profile/edit and /(tabs)/profile both held 'Loading profile…' for a fresh signup across repeated 5 s samples, exposing zero form testIDs, while /insights rendered normally on the same session.

defects.summary: Selecting the Trending tab throws an uncaught "Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'loading' in undefined" and blanks the whole application shell: 0 trending rows, not even the kit's empty state, and the always-mounted FeedScreen unmounts so Following and Global stop rendering until a full page reload. Cause: src/FeedScreen.tsx:113 reads existence(trending.read) where `trending` is a Read with no `.read` property.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-02 — src/FeedScreen.tsx:112-113; grading/evidence/shots/dbg-trending.png and shots/12-trending.png; six 5 s samples all read trending-rows=0, empty-state=0, body text length 0; clicking Global afterwards without a reload left the body length at 0.

defects.summary: The feeds never paginate. src/FeedScreen.tsx builds its page object with hasMore:false and loadMore:()=>{} and only ever queries api.home / api.globalFeed with c:null, so no continuation is ever followed and no 'Load more' affordance appears. The backend page size is also 40 rows, not the brief's pinned 20 per page.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m2-pagination — src/FeedScreen.tsx:16-25,141-145; snapback/schema.q home/globalFeed 'last 40 by .at after c'; both tabs rendered exactly 40 cards and stayed at 40 across 14 bottom scrolls with 0 'Load more' nodes, while the server cursor had 56 Following and 78 Global rows available.

defects.summary: The product has no in-chat ('messages within one chat') search scope, one of the brief's three pinned scopes. The only routed search screen offers All / People / Messages, takes no conversation argument and never calls api.searchChat; no conversation route exposes search.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m5-search — src/SearchScreen.tsx:19-66; api.searchChat is referenced only by src/Search.tsx, which is unrouted and does not typecheck; the live screen exposed exactly the scope labels ["All","People","Messages"].

defects.summary: Global message search is not grouped by chat. SearchScreen never sets the kit's groupLabel and never calls api.searchGrouped, so the kit renders a flat result list with no per-chat headers.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m5-search — src/SearchScreen.tsx:41-52,68-76; kit/src/SearchBar.tsx:100-108 emits sm-search-group only from item.groupLabel; searching 'coffee' produced 3 sm-search-result rows and 0 sm-search-group headers, while api.searchGrouped itself returns 2 correct per-conversation groups.

defects.summary: The Insights screen derives a lifetime total on the client by paging the corpus, which the brief explicitly forbids ('Totals are server-computed: the client never derives a total by paging the corpus'). It reads api.userPosts (declared 'last 100 by .at'), sums every row's likeCount, and renders Math.max(serverTotal, clientSum) — so it also understates for any author with more than 100 posts and transfers content to the client purely to compute a number.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-06 — src/InsightsScreen.tsx:15-18,42; snapback/schema.q query userPosts 'last 100 by .at'.

defects.summary: The scheduled digest job cannot complete at the scale envelope. During the scale replay it parked repeatedly with 'E_BOUND: examined rows reached the ceiling 16384'. digestTotals iterates every profile and, per profile, every membership and every follow edge with a nested message count, so examined rows grow with the product of users, memberships and follows.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-07 — logs/scale-backend.err lines 36-43: 'snapback4: job digest parked after 507 chunks: E_BOUND: examined rows reached the ceiling 16384' and two further parks, each with a matching 'dev refusal: digest ... code "E_BOUND"'; snapback/schema.q fn digestTotals / job digest.

defects.summary: The push seam was not disabled during the scale replay, contrary to the frozen replay contract ('The push seam is disabled during replay (a pinned replay-mode flag)') and M8's rule ('The push seam's replay-mode flag also disables digests during the scale replay'). The lane ships a backend:replay script but ran the scale backend without --replay, so the notifications worker and the 2-minute digest schedule fired throughout, emitting thousands of effects as replay side-effects.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#o5 — logs/scale-backend.err: worker started, 'schedule dailyDigest fired' repeatedly during the replay window with 'job digest done: 1007 chunks, 1000 rows written' and 'job digest done: 975 chunks, 1000 rows written'; package.json scripts.backend:replay exists but logs/scale-backend.err shows the plain 'snapback4 dev' banner on port 49362.

defects.summary: The scale replay performed none of the mandated end-state verification, and its evidence is now unreproducible. scripts/scale-replay.mjs never reads fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json, never pauses at the 10%/50% checkpoint markers to run probes, and never checks the named O5 fixtures (u0500's 500 follows, u0005, the celebrity u0900's 900 followers and 200 posts, u0901's 5-account following list, g0001's 50-member roster and 10,000 messages). The backend it ran against reported 'store: temporary — discarded on exit', so the end state no longer exists. The receipt records only settle-receipt accounting plus a hardcoded expected actionCount.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#o5 — scripts/scale-replay.mjs (no manifest read, no probe phase, checkpoints only record a settledPrefix); coverage/scale-replay-receipt.json (no invariant/conformance field, checkpoints 10% and 50% only, no 100%); logs/scale-backend.err line 6 'store: temporary — discarded on exit'; fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json expectedState.namedO5Fixtures.

defects.summary: Push-seam traffic is not observable at the documented path and is not durable. snapback/workers/notifications.mjs resolves its log relative to import.meta.url, but the worker executes from a per-process sandbox, so the log lands in .snapback4/worker-<rand>/scope/.../data/push-log.jsonl. The lane's own acceptance suite reads data/push-log.jsonl, which stayed 0 bytes through 67 logged payloads; the sandbox directory and its log are deleted when the backend stops, so every pre-restart payload is lost.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m6-push — snapback/workers/notifications.mjs:6-9; data/push-log.jsonl 0 bytes while .snapback4/worker-4hyZVb/scope/.../data/push-log.jsonl held 67 rows (55 push, 12 digest); after the mid-period restart that directory was gone and replaced by worker-XKOvIW with a fresh 3-row log.

defects.summary: The web Following feed intermittently still counts an unfollowed author's original as a direct follow-projection hit after an unfollow followed by a viewer-repost. Two of the harness's three attempts failed on exactly that assertion; the server-side projection is correct, so this is client-side staleness in the keep:false feed read combined with the optimistic repost override.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-12 — coverage/receipts-m2.jsonl 'repost-following-feed-surface' attempts 2 and 3: 'viewer-repost of an unfollowed author was counted as a direct follow-projection hit'; an independent 6-round API reproduction (unfollow -> repost -> read api.home) found 0 violations, each round showing exactly 1 viewer-repost row and 0 direct rows.

defects.summary: The history operation does not expose the brief's minimum message-object field manifest. api.history returns raw message rows with no reactions (emoji, count, caller's own state) and no receipt state for the caller's own messages; those require the separate api.messageReactions / api.reactionChips / api.messageReceipts operations. The brief pins the manifest as 'what the history operation must expose per message, so probes and the M7 snapshot are backend-neutral'.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m6 — snapback/schema.q query history ('messages where .conversation = conversation last 80 by byConversationOrdinal after c'); API.md 'Message object (history rows)' lists the fields and then directs receipts and reactions to separate handles.

defects.summary: API.md is incomplete for the grader variation it is meant to support. It does not document that api.inbox rows carry a chat object with a title (the only way to resolve a NAMED conversation), and it states no ordering for api.history pages, so 'the latest message' has to be inferred by inspecting rows. Both had to be discovered empirically.
defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#m6 — API.md Operations table and 'Message object (history rows)' section; the grader variation succeeded only after inspecting inbox rows for chat.title and sorting history rows by ordinal.

defects.summary: Six unrouted starter files remain in src/ (Feed.tsx, Profile.tsx, Chats.tsx, Conversation.tsx, Direct.tsx, Search.tsx) referencing API handles that do not exist in the generated surface (api.feed, api.post, api.profile, api.follow, api.createConversation, setLike({post})). defects.evidence: lanes/grok-snapback4/grading/trace.md#d-10 — grading/evidence/typecheck.txt; grep for searchChat/searchGrouped across src/ and app/ matches only src/Search.tsx.
